# SCI-FRUIT v0.1 — Qualification Access And Multiplicity Rules

Status: **Stage A candidate safeguards; no population or protocol selected**

## Prospective Access Plan

Before any qualification outcome is opened, an approved protocol must bind:

1. the maximum candidate family and complete hypothesis set;
2. the candidate submission deadline;
3. candidate/control label blinding and the exact unblinding event;
4. a prohibition on opening historical-control qualification outcomes before
   all candidate methods and decision rules are frozen;
5. whether qualification is one-shot or sequential;
6. whether and how the qualification population may ever be reused;
7. an exact alpha-spending or other sequential-monitoring rule, if applicable;
8. multiplicity handling across methods, profiles, metrics, scales, strata,
   and stopping policies;
9. joint confidence or hierarchical gatekeeping across protected and
   prioritized dimensions;
10. the minimum material effect and statistical-credibility construction; and
11. the independent replacement-population rule after an exploratory
    qualification result.

## Consequences Of Unblinding

A recurrence, feedback schema, parameter/adaptation policy, stopping policy,
metric, threshold, profile, domain, support rule, or failure rule changed after
qualification unblinding becomes a development candidate. It requires a new
identity and fresh untouched qualification evidence. An exploratory result
cannot be relabeled confirmatory.

Winner selection among several candidates must account for the selection
process; the selected winner does not inherit nominal single-candidate
uncertainty. Independent generations may be combined only by a rule frozen
before their outcomes are opened.

Qualification, development, and challenge populations are disjoint by exact
observation, injection, nuisance, source, and descendant-product lineage.
Near-duplicates and derived descendants cannot cross those boundaries.
